title: Delete Node in a BST
statement: Delete the node with the given key from the BST (if present) and return the new root. The result must still be a valid BST. (The checker accepts any valid result and compares in-order values.)

hints.1_question: There are three cases for the node to delete: no children, one child, two children. Which one is the tricky case?
hints.2_nudge: With two children, replace the node's value with its in-order successor (smallest value in the right subtree), then delete that successor from the right subtree.
hints.3_big_hint: Recurse by comparing key to root.val. When found: no left -> return right; no right -> return left; else copy successor value and delete it from root.right.

known_bugs.name: with two children, just keeps the left subtree
known_bugs.followup: When the deleted node has two children, what happens to its right subtree in your code?

known_bugs.name: copies the successor but never removes it
known_bugs.followup: After copying the successor's value up, how many nodes now hold that value?

known_bugs.name: assumes the key exists (no None check)
known_bugs.followup: What happens when the search runs off the bottom of the tree because the key isn't there?

followups: Could you use the in-order predecessor instead? Does it change correctness?
